s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with motor and speech impairment
salient_findings: Episodes of spasms and tremors in the right hand and forearm
key_facts: Woman in her mid-60s
Initial carpal tunnel release surgery
Recurring tremors
Referred to a neurologist 7 months later
Developed progressive right-sided weakness over 3 months
Brain MRI showed hyperintensities in bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter and other areas
No contrast enhancement on T1-weighted MRI
Brain biopsy showed CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ cells
Cerebrospinal fluid contained lymphoma cells
Bone marrow was negative for lymphoma cells

shortlist.label: Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Brain biopsy showed CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ cells and cerebrospinal fluid contained lymphoma cells

shortlist.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Brain MRI showed hyperintensities in bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter and other areas without contrast enhancement

shortlist.label: Multiple Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Brain MRI showed hyperintensities in bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter

shortlist.label: Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological decline with motor and speech impairment

shortlist.label: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive neurological decline with motor and speech impairment

shortlist.label: Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Brain MRI showed hyperintensities in bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter

shortlist.label: Intravascular Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Brain biopsy showed lymphoma cells and cerebrospinal fluid contained lymphoma cells

shortlist.label: Rasmussen Encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological decline with motor and speech impairment, and presence of lymphoma cells in cerebrospinal fluid

raw.rationale: The presence of lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid and the brain biopsy showing CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ cells strongly support this diagnosis, which is a type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma that primarily involves the brain and central nervous system.

rejected.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
rejected.why: This condition typically occurs in immunocompromised patients and is caused by the JC virus, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Multiple Sclerosis
rejected.why: The lack of contrast enhancement on MRI and the presence of lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis
rejected.why: This condition is typically monophasic and does not usually present with lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid.

rejected.label: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease
rejected.why: This condition is a prion disease that presents with rapidly progressive dementia, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with lobar hemorrhages, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Intravascular Lymphoma
rejected.why: This condition is a rare type of lymphoma that involves the blood vessels, but the brain biopsy and cerebrospinal fluid findings do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Rasmussen Encephalitis
rejected.why: This condition is a rare inflammatory disease that typically presents with seizures and hemiparesis, but the presence of lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid does not support this diagnosis.
